source.text: Here, There, Back

Here is Electra.

Here is Poz.

Here is the ball.

A red ball.

A blue ball.

There they are.

Electra reaches.

Poz reaches.

Toward the ball.

The red ball rolls.

It follows a path.

The ball is there.

Electra is here.

Poz is here.

Poz goes.

Hands, knees, go.

The blue ball rolls back.

Back to here.

Here.

There.

Back.

Again.

Here.
There.
Back.
Again.
Roll, Turn, Again

The floor is ready.

The red ball is still.

Electra gives one soft push.

Roll, ball, roll.

The ball does not hop.

It follows a path.

Up the little hill.

Slow, slow, slow.

The path turns.

The ball turns too.

Down in the little dip.

Round and round.

Poz catches the ball.

Stop, little ball.

Now the blue ball is still.

Will it go the same way?

Red went this way.

Blue went that way.

Roll.

Turn.

Again.

We learned the path.

Roll.
Turn.
Again.
Nature Remembers Motion

Electra pulled a ribbon.

The ribbon made a line.

Poz rolled the red ball.

The ball went away.

The ball was over there.

The trail was still here.

This part came first.

That part came next.

Some parts were close.

Some parts were far.

Electra tapped the water.

Circles grew from the tap.

Poz clapped.

Electra heard it after.

Poz walked past the light.

The shadow walked too.

Electra turned around.

The new trail met the old trail.

"Can we find where it went?"

Poz followed the trail.

Ribbon.

Water.

Sound.

Shadow.

They all showed motion.

It moved.

The world remembered.

Make a trail.
Follow it.
Again.
Again Makes A Pattern

Electra looked at yesterday's trail.

"What if we do it again?"

The red ball rolled across the floor.

One path appeared.

The blue ball rolled next.

Its path came close.

"It almost followed the first one,"

Electra said.

Poz moved the ball farther over.

The path changed.

Electra moved the ball near the old path.

The paths met.

One line crossed another.

Poz traced the crossing with one finger.

Roll.

Roll.

Roll.

The page grew busy.

The lines were not just anywhere.

They made a quiet shape.

"I think the next one goes here,"

Poz said.

They rolled once more.

The new path joined the shape.

Again made a pattern.

The pattern helped them see.

Roll again.
Find the pattern.
What Changed?

Electra watched the red ball roll.

"Why did the ball go there?"

The red ball rolled from the star.

It stopped in the dip.

Poz drew the path.

"This is what happened."

"If we try again,"

Electra asked,

"where will it go?"

Same start.

Same push.

Same path.

Poz changed one thing.

Only one.

The ball rolled again.

This time it turned left.

Old path.

New path.

What changed?

They swapped in a hill.

The ball slowed near the top.

They tried a flat path.

The ball rolled straight through.

Electra pointed.

"The path changes when the ball meets something new."

"What should we change next?"

Poz asked.

Change one thing.
Compare what happened.
The Message That Traveled

Electra heard the clock.

Tick came before.

Tock came after.

Poz clapped across the yard.

Electra saw Poz's hands.

Then Electra heard the clap.

"The clap was real,"

Electra said,

"but it was not everywhere at once."

Poz stood by the tree.

The clap began there.

Electra dropped a pebble.

Rings ran away from the splash.

A leaf floated on the water.

The ring reached it.

The leaf moved.

Poz tapped the near bell.

Electra heard it quickly.

Poz tapped the far bell.

Electra listened.

Then it rang.

Electra pointed from bell to ear.

"The message came across here."

Poz pushed a toy boat.

A little wake opened behind it.

The wake touched a paper leaf.

The leaf slid away.

Clap.

Ring.

Ripple.

Roll.

Each one traveled.

"A message can be on the way,"

Electra said,

"before it reaches me."

Begin.
Travel.
Arrive.

Begin.
Travel.
Arrive.
Patterns That Hold

Electra set three beads on strings.

Poz gave one bead a gentle push.

One bead swung too far.

The pattern broke apart.

One bead barely moved.

Nothing interesting lasted.

Electra tried a smaller push.

The beads moved.

Then moved again together.

Left.

Right.

Left.

The pattern came back.

"It is holding,"

Poz said.

"But nothing is frozen."

Each bead pulled on another.

Each answer came at the right time.

Poz moved one bead farther away.

The old rhythm faded.

Electra moved it back.

The rhythm returned.

Electra watched.

"Later, we can call this kind of holding an assembly."

Three beads held.

Then four.

Then five.

The parts kept moving.

The relation held.

Nature can build with motion.

Move.
Fit.
Hold.

Move.
Fit.
Hold.
The Tiny Transceivers

Electra and Poz opened the message lab.

Their question was small and enormous:

What sends the deepest messages?

Electra placed one red point on the screen.

It moved.

They could follow its path.

Then Poz placed one blue point.

"This is the other kind,"

Poz said.

A card on the screen said:

architrino.

Electra read the word slowly.

The red architrino moved.

From its old place, a message began.

The blue architrino crossed the screen.

When the message reached it,

its path changed.

"It is not just a flash,"

Poz said.

"It has a before and after."

Red and blue did not answer the same way.

Their paths bent differently.

One pair bent inward.

The children called it toward.

Another pair bent outward.

The children called it away.

"Red is not angry,"

Electra said.

"Blue is not calm."

The lab filled with red and blue points.

Every one kept its own path.

Each tiny point could send.

Each tiny point could receive.

The room became a web of messages.

"Tiny does not mean simple,"

Poz said.

"Tiny can carry the rules."

Path.
Send.
Receive.

Path.
Send.
Receive.
